critique_of_gto_peer: GTO peer's 88/12 is well-grounded on equity-realization, IP-closing, and pot-odds arithmetic; their crucial addition is the observation that AKo's blocker profile is poor for raising (blocks AQ/AJ that fold anyway, blocks KQ/AK that call). That blocker-direction critique is the strongest argument against my 30% raise slice, and I accept it partially. Where I push back: GTO peer slightly under-weights the range-construction need for a balancing raise slice in BTN's continuing range — even if AdKd is sub-optimal as the bluff-raise selector, SOME hand must occupy that slot, and the combinatorics of KT/T9s/JTs combos may be too thin to carry the entire raise frequency alone. Net effect on me: shift from 70/30 toward 80/20.
critique_of_multiway_peer: Multiway peer's 80/20 is the closest to mine and the most rigorous on per-villain composition. Their key insight — that CO is the structural problem not because of squeeze pressure but because CO's range-cap geometry makes CO densely concentrated in JT/T9/KTs/QJs/sets that smash QJ9, so a hero raise gets called or 3-bet by exactly the hands that crush AdKd — is the sharpest argument in the panel. They also correctly note KTs/T9s/JTs are the proper raise-selectors (hand-class equity + straight-removal blockers), not AdKd. I accept this fully and it pushes my raise slice down from 30% to ~18-20%.
critique_of_sonnet_split: CALL voters (Labeller 1, 2, 3): converge tightly on pot odds + nut-gutshot + IP realization + CO-sandwich risk = CALL, mostly HIGH confidence. Labeller 2 explicitly cites mix ~75/25 which aligns with the consensus band. Their arguments are clean and consistent with my position. RAISE voters (Labellers 4, 5): both reach for the semi-bluff-with-nut-equity narrative and 3.6x sizing. Labeller 4 incorrectly treats CO as 'still to act behind' on the raise (CO already acted by flatting/calling MP's c-bet in 3-way order: MP-CO-BTN), inflating fold-equity expectations. Labeller 5's case rests on CO having 'many call-and-raise hands' — which actually argues AGAINST raising AdKd into that range, not for it. Both RAISE voters under-weight the range-cap-but-strong CO composition that the multiway peer surfaces.
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus tier-up RAISE-to-9bb at MEDIUM confidence overstates the case. Two specific errors: (1) Opus claims raw equity vs MP's c-bet range is ~48-52% — inflated; multiway peer's mid-30s estimate is more honest once Qx+/overpairs/sets/straights/two-pair are properly weighted in MP's continuing range, and the 3-way CO presence drags realization further. (2) Opus claims raise 'folds CO's capped continuance' — but CO already called the c-bet, so CO's range is now the strong-continue subset (JT/T9/KTs/QJs/sets/big-draws) which precisely does NOT fold to a flop raise and disproportionately 3-bets it. Opus's MEDIUM-confidence flag is honest acknowledgment that the mix is close, but the directional call (RAISE as modal) is wrong against CO's post-call composition.
revised_reasoning: I move from CALL MED 70/30 to CALL HIGH 82/18. The peer debate convinced me on two specific points without overturning my modal action. First, multiway peer's structural argument is decisive: CO already called MP's c-bet, so CO's range at hero's decision node is the strong-continue subset — sets, two-pair, made straights KT/T8s, big combo-draws JT/T9/QTs — and this range does not fold to a hero raise. It calls or 3-bets, and exactly the 3-bet portion crushes AdKd's semi-bluff equity. My R1 acknowledged CO as 'the structural problem' but I framed it as squeeze-jam/cold-call risk pre-raise; the sharper framing is post-call composition risk. Second, GTO peer's blocker-direction point on AKo is correct: blocking AQ/AJ removes folds, blocking KQ/AK keeps calls — AdKd is a poor raise-selector from this slice. The proper raise combos are KTs (straight-blocker + made), T9s/JTs (pair + OESD + blocker), KsQs-type FD-blockers. AdKd lacks both made-equity and straight-removal, so it belongs in the CALL slice even if the slice exists. On balance: BTN's continuing range DOES need a raise slice for game-theoretic balance (KT/AT-value + KTs/JTs/T9s-semi-bluff), but pure CALL with AdKd specifically is sustainable without exploitability because the bluff-raise slot is better-filled by hands carrying made-equity-plus-straight-blockers. Revising AdKd to CALL 82% / RAISE 18% (down from 30%): the 18% represents combinatorial residue — if KT/T9s/JTs combos can't carry the full balancing raise frequency alone, AdKd is the next-best A-blocker semi-bluff selector. But the modal action is unambiguously CALL, and confidence rises to HIGH given panel unanimity at the action level and convergence of per-villain composition arguments. The R1 priority ordering (CO-sandwich over semi-bluff-by-structure) was correct; R2 sharpens it from 'sandwich risk pre-raise' to 'CO post-call range crushes AdKd specifically'.
